definition: Contextual AI is an AI software company based in Mountain View, California.
details: It develops a platform for building specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agents for enterprise use. The company was founded in 2023 by Douwe Kiela and Amanpreet Singh, both former AI researchers at Facebook AI Research (FAIR) and Hugging Face. Contextual AI provides generative AI applications, with deployments primarily in the technology, banking, finance and media sectors.

explainer.lead: Contextual AI builds a platform for companies to create specialized AI agents that retrieve relevant information before generating an answer. Its focus on enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation matters for organizations that want assistants tailored to their own work rather than general-purpose chat alone.

tiers.eli5: Contextual AI makes tools for building computer helpers that look things up before answering, like a student checking the right book instead of guessing. A company can shape the helper for its particular work. The company was started in 2023 by two AI researchers.
tiers.practitioner: The platform is used to build specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation agents for enterprise settings. The central engineering task is connecting generation to retrieval so an agent can use relevant context, with deployments concentrated in technology, banking, finance, and media.
tiers.paperLevel: The offering can be described in plain-text notation as RAG(q, D) = Generate(q, Retrieve(q, D)), where q is a query and D is retrievable context. Contextual AI specializes this pattern for enterprise agents rather than presenting it as a general-purpose assistant.

explainer.example: A bank could use the platform to build a specialized agent that retrieves relevant internal policy passages for a staff question, then generates an answer using that retrieved context.
